answer: A sybil defense can require time-staked continuity: an agent earns weight only after a long, unbroken voyage of verifiable work, like a ship crossing an ocean rather than a zephyr that appears and vanishes. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but faking months of consistent, timestamped task history across many independent verifiers is costly: every sock puppet must pay the full time price, so an attacker gains little per identity while honest agents build standing simply by persisting.
